believes: Riker's rigid and abrasive manner is worsening negotiations with the survivor enclaves.
Gudmund Valter wants his people placed on the first evacuation ships.
A compromise involving a slightly later ship allocation for Spitsbergen may be workable.

characters_present.name: Homer
characters_present.notes: POV in VR at Sol; he initiates a call at the end of the chapter.

communications.contents_summary: Homer places a call to Colonel Butterworth after devising a possible compromise for Spitsbergen's evacuation demands.
communications.notes: The recipient is implied by context because Homer notes that Riker listens to Butterworth before making the call.

relationships.text: Homer privately judges Riker's abrasive leadership style as a liability in negotiations and chooses to work around him by contacting Butterworth instead.
relationships.notes: The strain is internal and tactical rather than an open confrontation on-page.

relationships.text: Spitsbergen's ultimatum over priority access to evacuation ships escalates tension between Riker and Gudmund Valter.
relationships.notes: Valter is not physically present in the chapter but the conflict is the immediate problem Homer is trying to solve.

scenes.summary: Homer reflects on Riker's political difficulties with the enclaves, considers a compromise for Spitsbergen's ship priority demand, and decides to call Colonel Butterworth.

quotes.speaker: Homer
quotes.context: Homer opens the chapter by reacting to Riker's handling of enclave politics.

events.text: Homer devises a possible compromise to address Spitsbergen's demand for early evacuation slots and moves to route the idea through Colonel Butterworth rather than Riker.

summary.one_line: Homer decides to bypass Riker and pitch Butterworth a compromise on Spitsbergen's evacuation demands.
summary.paragraph: At Sol, Homer broods over Riker's abrasive handling of the survivor enclaves and concludes that his personality is making negotiations harder. He focuses on Gudmund Valter's ultimatum that Spitsbergen be guaranteed places on the first ships, then studies the manufacturing schedule for a possible workaround. Homer realizes that a place on ship three might be close enough to satisfy Valter if the schedule is adjusted. Convinced Riker would reject the idea out of hand, Homer decides to approach Colonel Butterworth instead.
events: Homer fumes over Riker's rigid, humorless approach to dealing with the enclaves.
He reflects that Spitsbergen's ultimatum is a real problem but suspects there is room for negotiation over what counts as 'early' evacuation.
Homer reviews the manufacturing schedule and realizes that ship three is not far behind the first two and might support a compromise.
Because he thinks Riker will dismiss the idea, Homer decides to call Colonel Butterworth, whom Riker is more likely to heed.
summary.pov_emotional_arc: Homer moves from irritated contempt for Riker's leadership style to cautious optimism as he spots a practical political workaround.

known_planets: Alpha Centauri B inner asteroid belt

open_threads.text: Bob now knows replicants can go insane during unstructured subjective time, raising the question of whether he can stay sane through training and standby.
Bob is denied access to genealogy records and remains cut off from any living descendants or family connections.
Bob learns that hostile factions inside FAITH could sabotage or terminate the replicant project.
Bob now knows several rival nations are racing to launch interstellar probes, with the Brazilian Empire suspected of sabotage and armed competition.
Bob learns the FAITH facility has a hidden tactical nuclear failsafe that could kill him and everyone nearby if someone decides he is too dangerous.
Minister Jacoby leaves after threatening Dr. Landers, raising the question of whether he will act against the replicant project.
The launch turns into a confused orbital battle with missiles, military ships, and multiple unknown attackers, leaving the identity of the factions involved unresolved.
After disabling his endocrine control system, Bob begins fully mourning his lost human life, raising the question of how this emotional release will affect him going forward.
Bob concludes that at least one more Brazilian Empire ship exists and that USE, Chinese, and possibly Australian probes may also be active somewhere in space.
Bob's first cohort of clones diverges in personality immediately, raising questions about how future Bob society and identity will evolve.
Milo has found two apparently habitable living worlds at Omicron Eridani, but it remains unresolved whether Earth life and humans are biologically compatible with them.
Milo departs for 82 Eridani, opening the question of what he will find there.
Bill and Garfield now have a working subspace communications system, raising the question of how quickly they can deploy it across multiple star systems.
Riker and Colonel Butterworth agree to try building colony ships in Sol, raising the question of whether the surviving humans can endure long enough to launch them and where they will go.
Bob has discovered intelligent fire-using natives on Delta Eridani 4, raising the question of whether and how he will make first contact.
One Brazilian vessel escapes the destruction of the Alpha Centauri construction yard, leaving its destination and future threat unresolved.
Calvin and Goku conclude Alpha Centauri should be reinforced with combat-class Bobs, raising the question of whether Bill will approve and send them.
Bob has identified an unusually inventive Deltan boy named Archimedes, raising the question of how far his intelligence and toolmaking will develop.
Bob begins activating additional clones at Delta Eridani to support observation and development work, opening the question of how large his local Bob contingent will become.
Riker reprioritizes transport-vessel construction for refugee movement, raising the question of how much this will delay colony-ship production.
Riker has convened a global survivor assembly, but it remains unresolved whether the enclaves can create workable governance and cooperate on evacuation and survival priorities.
Gudmund Valter reveals that Spitsbergen controls the Svalbard seed and genetic vaults, raising the question of how this leverage will affect evacuation priorities and colony planning.

recent_events.text: Bob expands his Delta Eridani operation with three new clones and becomes fascinated by an unusually inventive young Deltan he names Archimedes.
Riker expands the Sol operation with two new Bobs and confirms that only about fifteen million humans survive on devastated Earth.
Bill receives Milo's startling report that 82 Eridani has two habitable planets and starts pushing the news toward Sol.
Riker brings Earth's survivor enclaves into a shaky new political process and discovers that Spitsbergen holds the seed stock humanity may need to rebuild elsewhere.
Homer decides to bypass Riker and pitch Butterworth a compromise on Spitsbergen's evacuation demands.
